name: Hindi
description: One of India's most widely spoken languages, used in literature, cinema, education and everyday communication.

name: Punjabi
speakers: Over 30 million native speakers in India
description: A vibrant language associated with Punjab's folk traditions, poetry, music and rich literary heritage.

name: Kashmiri
description: A language of the Kashmir Valley, known for its poetry, Sufi traditions and distinctive literary heritage.

name: Dogri
description: Spoken mainly in the Jammu region, Dogri has a strong tradition of folk songs, storytelling and poetry.

name: Sanskrit
speakers: Small number of everyday speakers; extensive scholarly and liturgical use
description: An ancient classical language of India, central to many Hindu, Buddhist and Jain philosophical and literary traditions.

name: Urdu
description: Known for its poetic expression, ghazals, literary traditions and rich vocabulary.

name: Bhojpuri
description: Popular in eastern Uttar Pradesh and western Bihar, with a strong tradition of folk music and cinema.

name: Awadhi
description: A literary language associated with the Awadh region and the celebrated epic Ramcharitmanas.

name: Rajasthani
description: A group of related language varieties known for folk ballads, oral storytelling and regional literature.

name: Gujarati
description: The principal language of Gujarat, with a rich literary history and a strong tradition of trade and theatre.

name: Marathi
description: Spoken mainly in Maharashtra, Marathi has a distinguished tradition of poetry, theatre and modern literature.

name: Konkani
description: A coastal language spoken especially in Goa and parts of the Konkan region, shaped by diverse cultural influences.

name: Sindhi
description: A language with a rich Sufi, folk and literary tradition, spoken by communities across India.

name: Malayalam
description: The principal language of Kerala, recognised for its literature, cinema, poetry and distinctive script.

name: Tamil
speakers: Over 60 million native speakers in India
description: A classical language with an ancient literary tradition, including Sangam poetry and celebrated Tamil epics.

name: Telugu
description: A major Dravidian language spoken in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, famous for its literary and cinematic traditions.

name: Kannada
description: The principal language of Karnataka, with a literary history spanning more than a thousand years.

name: Tulu
description: Spoken mainly in coastal Karnataka and parts of Kerala, known for its folk theatre and ritual traditions.

name: Kodava
description: A language of the Kodagu region of Karnataka, closely connected with the community's distinctive cultural traditions.

name: Gondi
script: Several scripts, including Gunjala Gondi and Devanagari
description: An important language of Gond communities across central India, with a rich oral heritage.

name: Bengali
speakers: Over 90 million native speakers in India
description: A major literary language associated with Rabindranath Tagore, poetry, music and the Bengal Renaissance.

name: Assamese
description: The principal language of Assam, with a strong tradition of literature, theatre and devotional music.

name: Odia
description: The principal language of Odisha, recognised for its classical literature and devotional poetry.

name: Santali
description: An important Munda language with a rich oral tradition, folk music and community literature.

name: Bodo
description: A major language of Assam's Bodo community, with a growing body of modern literature.

name: Manipuri (Meitei)
description: The principal language of Manipur, known for its classical dance, poetry and cultural heritage.

name: Mizo
description: The principal language of Mizoram, with a strong tradition of community singing and literature.

name: Khasi
description: Spoken mainly in Meghalaya, Khasi has a rich oral tradition and is closely tied to local cultural identity.

name: Garo
description: A language spoken by Garo communities, especially in Meghalaya, with a strong oral and folk tradition.

name: Lepcha
description: An indigenous Himalayan language spoken in parts of Sikkim and neighbouring regions, with its own traditional script.
